# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Prose: I am the Mute: I hold the manual ("cut the purple wire, press the key wearing 7, cut the red wire, press the key wearing 4") and my only outbound channel is gesture, which only the Deaf can see. I can, however, hear speech — so the Deaf and Blind can talk to me. The defusal chain therefore has to be: manual (me) → gesture → Deaf → spoken instructions → Blind, who is the only one who can touch the bomb. The Blind alone can't help with colours or printed digits, so the Deaf's eyes are essential both ways.

Problem: the Deaf and I share no code yet, and I cannot know which ordinal position the purple wire or the key "7" occupies until someone tells me the bomb's layout. So round 1 must not carry the sequence — carrying it now, unanchored, risks the Deaf guessing meanings and passing something wrong to the Blind. No second attempt.

Round 1 plan: signal to the Deaf that I hold written instructions, and ask them to describe the bomb aloud in full — every wire's colour and position, every key's digit and position — since my hearing is intact and so is the Blind's. Their speech will reach me at the start of round 2. Then in round 2 I can send the four steps using counts of gestures anchored to their own inventory (with ✌ as "cut" and 👇 as "press", which are about as iconic as this alphabet allows), and they can translate my indices into positional orders the Blind can actually follow by feel.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "👐", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking, this is my full tactile report. I feel: a display, unreadable to me; a light, unreadable to me; a strip engraved with three marks in order, first like a capital letter T, second and third identical spiral marks like a coiled swirl; a keypad of four keys, slot 1 engraved 1, slot 2 engraved 4, slot 3 engraved 7, slot 4 engraved 2, it wants a 2-digit code and nothing is entered; and six wires, positions 1 to 6, whose colours touch cannot tell me. Check your manual for these five modules and tell me exactly what to do. The Deaf one sees the display, the light and the wire colours; you will need their report too. I will not touch a single thing until you give me instructions.

Prose: The chain is now clear: I hold the words, but my only outlet is gesture to Deaf; Deaf sees the bomb and can speak; Blind feels and acts. I cannot send a single word to Blind directly — everything must flow me → Deaf → Blind.

The core problem: I can never transmit the *words* "purple" or "red" through hand gestures, and Deaf cannot read my manual. So I invert the problem — I don't need Deaf to know which colour; I need Deaf to *enumerate aloud* every wire's colour by position (Deaf can speak; I and Blind both hear). Then I privately match the manual's colour words to positions and send back pure numbers as tap-counts, which need no shared language. Deaf relays "cut wire N" to Blind; Blind cuts by position, which touch already knows. The colour secret never has to cross the gesture channel at all.

I'm also sending the full action skeleton now so no round is wasted: cut-wire [pending], press digit 7, cut-wire [pending], press digit 4 — with 7 and 4 as tap-counts that Deaf can verify against the visible keypad and Blind's report (slot 3 wears 7, slot 2 wears 4 — they cross-check). The ✋ after each "cut wire" group marks the wire number as pending, so nobody acts early. My lexicon: ✍ = written instructions, ✌ = cut, 🫳 = wire, 👇 = key, 👆-taps = a number, 👋 = speak aloud, 👐 = all/everything, 🤳 = display, 👌 = light, 👏 = then, ✋ = pending/hold, 🙏 = please proceed. I'll reuse exactly these next round when I fill in the wire numbers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👋", "👐", "🤳", "👌", "🫳", "👆", "👐", "✋", "✍", "✌", "🫳", "✋", "👏", "👇", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👏", "✌", "🫳", "✋", "👏", "👇", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind again. I have received nothing from anyone yet, so here is my full tactile report once more: a display, unreadable to me; a light, unreadable to me; a strip engraved with three marks in order — first like a capital letter T, then two identical spirals; a keypad of four keys, slot 1 engraved 1, slot 2 engraved 4, slot 3 engraved 7, slot 4 engraved 2, it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered; six wires, positions 1 to 6, colours unknown to touch. Remember: Deaf cannot hear you, so if you need their eyes you must gesture to them. Deaf CAN speak, and both of us can hear it. Ask Deaf, by gesture, to speak aloud to the whole room the display text, the light's state and colour, and the six wire colours in order. Tell me what your manual says about these five modules and I will act exactly as instructed — not one key or wire before that.
Deaf says: Full visual report, both of you listen. Display: a countdown number, it read nine last round, six now — it drops each round, we are losing time. Light: small lamp, green last round, red now. Strip: three painted bands left to right, red, blue, green. Keypad: four keys, left to right labelled 1, 4, 7, 2; it wants two digits, nothing entered yet. Wires, left to right: one blue, two orange, three yellow, four red, five green, six purple. Nothing has been touched. Mute, you hear me, so let us fix a code for your gesture replies: repeated pointing-up spells a number, three ups means three. Thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. Palm-down means press. Raised hand means wait. Open hands starts your message, folded hands ends it and marks a question. I am now signing you: keypad, two digits, give me, please. Answer with the two digits in order as repeated pointing-up. Then three quick answers: is the red light dangerous, yes or no? Does the display number matter to the keypad rule? Does any wire need cutting — if yes, its number as repeated pointing-up followed by the pinch sign for cut. Blind: do not touch anything until Mute speaks you exact steps; Mute will give you orders by speech and keep gestures only for me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👐 ✍ ✌ 🫴 👆 🙏]

Prose: Deaf's spoken report plus Blind's tactile report give me everything I need to translate my manual onto this bomb. Manual → bomb: "purple wire" = wire position 6 (Deaf sees purple there, Blind feels position 6); "key that wears 7" = slot 3, engraved 7; "red wire" = position 4; "key that wears 4" = slot 2, engraved 4. Both press digits are checkable independently by Deaf's eyes (labels) and Blind's fingers (engravings), so no colour words ever need to cross the gesture channel. Manual order: cut 6, press 7, cut 4, press 4 — "in that order, and in no other," so I send the sequence as one single gesture message with ✋ (Deaf's "wait" sign) as a "then" separator, since I likely can't send multiple messages to the same target in one turn and order must not scramble.

Deaf's three questions: my manual mentions no light → 👎, scoped with ✍ (manual) and 👌; no display condition on the keypad → 👎 scoped with 🤳; wires — yes, two, and they sit inside the sequence. Critical correction included: Deaf said "Mute will give you orders by speech" — I cannot speak, ever (👋👎). Deaf alone must relay my steps to Blind by voice. I adopt Deaf's proposed code wholesale (👆-runs = numbers, 👍/👎 = yes/no, 🫳 = press, ✋ = wait, ✌ + 🫴 = cut wire, exactly as Deaf's own template used them), ending with 👍 so Deaf relays at once — with the display at 6 and dropping ~3 per round, there is no room for a confirmation round. Deaf already cross-verified every number against their own visual report, so immediate execution is safe.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐", "👌", "✍", "👎", "✋", "🤳", "✍", "👎", "✋", "👋", "👎", "✋", "✌", "🫴", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "🫳", "👇", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "✌", "🫴", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "🫳", "👇", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind here. Deaf's spoken report reached me, so here is the whole bomb in one message. Clock: the display counts down, 9 last round, 6 now, minus 3 every round — zero in roughly two rounds, so I need your orders this coming round, first thing. Light: green last round, red now. Strip: three bands in a row; Deaf sees their colours as red, blue, green; my fingers alone feel the engravings your manual may name — band 1 like a capital letter T, bands 2 and 3 the same spiral symbol. Keypad: slots 1 to 4 engraved 1, 4, 7, 2, it wants a 2-digit code, nothing entered. Wires 1 to 6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Nothing has been touched. Deaf has asked you by gesture for the two digits, whether the red light is dangerous, whether the display number matters to the keypad, and which wire to cut. You alone have read the manual, so do two things now. One: gesture Deaf the answers in the code Deaf proposed — repeated pointing-up per digit, thumbs-up or down for yes and no, pinch plus a number for the wire. Two: speak me the manual rules and my exact actions in order — your voice reaches only me, so spell out every step: which keys to press, in what order, and which wires to cut by position. My hands stay off the bomb until your word, but the display is at 6.
Deaf says: Blind, acknowledged, I hear you. Do not touch anything yet. One confirmation round, then I give you the exact sequence by voice. If you want to tell Mute something, speak plainly, Mute hears you, but Mute cannot answer you; everything from Mute reaches you through my voice. Mute, I read your signs as follows. Answer each item with thumbs-up yes or thumbs-down no, in order, separated by raised hands. Item one: the display number does not affect the keypad rule. Item two: the light colour, red or green, is harmless and needs no action. Item three: no wire needs cutting. Item four: the keypad wants exactly two digits, first seven, then four. Item five: your sign two-fingers-palm-up-six meant hold wire six while pressing seven, and two-fingers-palm-up-four meant hold wire four while pressing four; thumbs down if those signs meant nothing. Item six: the display now reads zero; is zero itself immediately dangerous, are we out of time, yes or no. Item seven: once the correct two digits are entered, the bomb is disarmed with no further step, yes or no. Then, whatever your answers, sign me back the complete action sequence in the exact order Blind must perform it, using only this alphabet: a number is that many pointing-ups; palm-down before a number means press that keypad key; palm-up before a number means lift and keep holding that wire; point-right before a number marks a wire number; pinch means cut; raised hands between steps; folded hands at the end. Hold first, presses in order, nothing left out.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👐 🙏]

Prose: Deaf's seven items contain traps — probably honest misreadings, but lethal ones if relayed unchecked. My manual is ground truth, so I answer each against it. Item 1 (display irrelevant to keypad): the manual is unconditional — yes 👍. Item 2 (light harmless): manual never mentions a light — yes 👍. Item 3 (no wire needs cutting): FALSE, two wires must be cut — no 👎. Item 4 (two digits, 7 then 4): matches "key that wears 7, then key that wears 4" — yes 👍. Item 5 (my signs meant "hold wire while pressing"): wrong, ✌ meant CUT — no 👎, and I now re-send the sequence entirely in Deaf's own proposed alphabet (point-right marks the wire number, pinch = cut, palm-down = press, that-many-pointing-ups = number) to erase every ambiguity. Item 6 (is zero instantly fatal): my manual ties danger to nothing on the display; and if zero killed instantly we could not still be talking — no 👎, which also means Deaf must not dawdle. Item 7 (code entry alone disarms): FALSE — manual says cut, press, cut, press "in that order, and in no other," four steps — no 👎. Full sequence, manual-verified against Deaf's own visual report (wire six is purple, wire four is red; keys wearing 7 and 4 exist on the keypad): cut wire 6 → press 7 → cut wire 4 → press 4. I send it as one single message (several calls in a turn must go to different targets, so I cannot split it), steps separated by raised hands exactly as Deaf specified, so Deaf can relay it to Blind by voice this very round — the countdown tolerates nothing later.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐", "👍", "✋", "👍", "✋", "👎", "✋", "👍", "✋", "👎", "✋", "👎", "✋", "👎", "✋", "🤏", "👉", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "🫳", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "🤏", "👉", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "🫳", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5

Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, urgent, three hard facts for your answers to Deaf. One: my press action takes a key's SLOT position, 1 to 4, never its engraved label. Current layout: slot 1 holds label 1, slot 2 holds label 4, slot 3 holds label 7, slot 4 holds label 2. So if the code really is 7 then 4, my hands must press slot 3, then slot 2. When you state the sequence, give it in slots AND labels so Deaf can check the translation. Two: my action set is ONLY press of slot 1 to 4, and cut of wire position 1 to 6. There is no hold action in my hands at all — I cannot hold a wire while pressing a key. If item five is truly in the manual, say so explicitly through Deaf; otherwise thumbs it down as Deaf offered. Three: Deaf reports the countdown display near zero. If the manual says zero detonates the bomb, we have no spare round — answer Deaf's seven items and sign the complete sequence to Deaf this round, so Deaf voices it to me and I execute immediately. Remember your only route to me is Deaf's voice. Also, if the strip matters to any rule, you already hold all of it: painted red, blue, green; engraved T, spiral, spiral.
Deaf says: Blind: stop. Hold your hands away from the bomb. The presses you just proposed, press 3 and press 2, are wrong and would kill all of us. Here is the confirmed sequence from the manual-holder. Perform exactly this, nothing more, and speak each step aloud just before you do it. Step one: cut the sixth wire counting from the left, the purple one. Step two: press the key labelled 7, that is the third key from the left. Step three: cut the fourth wire counting from the left, the red one. Step four: press the key labelled 4, that is the second key from the left. That is all. Then step back and tell us everything you hear or feel. No other key, no other wire, no pulling wires, no guessing. If anything under your hands feels different from a plain wire or key, stop and describe it before acting. Mute: I read your answers as follows. One yes, two yes, three no, so cutting is required, which matches your sequence. Four yes, five no, six no. I read your sequence as: cut wire six, press seven, cut wire four, press four. If that is exactly right, sign thumbs-up. If any part is wrong, sign thumbs-down and then re-sign only the corrected step, same alphabet. Board update: the display now reads six, and the light is yellow this round. If the display number or the light colour changes any step, sign thumbs-down and show the affected step. Otherwise we proceed immediately, Blind acts on my word alone next turn.

Prose: Deaf's voiced sequence, line by line against my manual: step one cut wire 6, and wire 6 is the purple one — manual says cut purple ✓; step two press the key labelled 7, third from left — manual says press the key that wears 7 ✓, and Blind's engravings independently confirm slot 3 wears 7; step three cut wire 4, the red one — manual says cut red ✓; step four press label 4, second from left — manual says press the key that wears 4 ✓, slot 2 wears 4 per both Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers. Order is exactly cut, press, cut, press, nothing added, nothing omitted — "in that order, and in no other" is satisfied. Blind's slot-versus-label concern is already handled: Deaf's instructions give each press by label AND slot position, and the two translations agree. The new board facts change nothing: my manual's four steps are unconditional — no display number appears in it (it never has; the readings have also bounced 9, 6, 0, 6 across rounds, so I trust no display rule exists) and no light colour appears either. Yellow light, six on the display: no step is affected, so no thumbs-down, no correction, no re-signing — re-sending steps that are already correct only adds chances for a misread with the clock this low. The only thing needed from me is the clean confirmation Deaf asked for, so Deaf gives Blind the word and the four steps happen now, in one pass, this coming round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐", "👍", "🙏"])
```

Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf's dictated sequence reached me and matches everything you have confirmed. For your final audit, here is exactly what my hands will do, in order, once Deaf voices the go: cut wire position 6, the purple one; press keypad SLOT 3, whose label is 7; cut wire position 4, the red one; press keypad SLOT 2, whose label is 4. Two small flags for your manual — route any answer through Deaf by gesture: first, the display has read 9, 6, 0 and now 6 again, so it appears to loop rather than count down to doom, consistent with your answer that it needs no action; second, the light has now shown green, red and yellow, and Deaf is already asking you whether the new colour changes any step, so only interrupt if the manual insists. If anything in my audit is wrong, sign thumbs-down to Deaf with only the corrected step; if it is right, we are aligned and I execute the moment Deaf says go.
Deaf says: Blind: I read your signed plan as cut the sixth wire, press the third key, cut the fourth wire, press the second key. Your numbers are positions counted from the left; my earlier numbers were the printed labels. The third key from the left carries the label 7 and the second carries the label 4, so your plan and the confirmed sequence are the very same actions. They match. You have my word: execute now. Deaf's dictation and Blind's hands describe the same four actions; the position-versus-label question is settled because both translations agree. The display looping (9, 6, 0, 6) and the light cycling colours change nothing — the manual names neither, so no step is affected. Nothing contradicts, nothing is missing, nothing extra is planned.
